themes.name: AI compute: NVIDIA's supply chain
themes.what: Nvidia reported after the close on Nov 17: quarterly revenue $115.84 billion, up 103.2% from a year ago, with data center revenue $107.60 billion (up 110%) and adjusted EPS $2.68. It guided this quarter to $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, against about $125.25 billion expected (LSEG via Reuters). It logged $2.4 billion of licensed Hopper sales to China in the quarter, will ship no more, and the guide includes none (Investing.com). NVDA rose about 2.7% to 3.7% before Wednesday's open; AMD, AVGO, MU and MRVL rose 1.9% to 3.2% premarket (Reuters).
themes.for_you: The demand side of the chain held up: the guide rose about $22 billion in one quarter. But China is now zero in the guide and the chip license rule is still coming, so the risk moved from demand to policy. Long term: ANET (186.42) and ADI (383.67) held their points through the report; ADI still reports Nov 24 (unconfirmed). Wait for Wednesday's close on volume before any first piece.

themes.name: GLP-1 and obesity
themes.what: CMS proposed a rule (CMS-6098-P, the 'CRUSH' proposal) on Nov 16 that would audit Medicare Advantage risk adjustment data without a fee for service adjuster and extrapolate findings back to payment year 2018; CMS estimates about $9 billion recovered per payment year. Comments are due Jan 19, 2027, and nothing applies until a final rule (GuruFocus; Barchart). Insurers fell Nov 17: UNH -5.42% to 389.68, ELV -2.77% to 433.93, CI -2.03% to 294.06, and Humana and CVS more than 3% (Massive; Barchart).
themes.for_you: This hits the plans that pay for GLP-1 drugs, not the drug makers. CI sits 0.8% over its range low (291.57, alert live) and 2.0% over its long term point (288.26), rated 'Wait' because sellers outweigh buyers. No new puts on insurers until a comment period this long settles; a confirmed close under 291.57 on 2,434,000+ shares would block them anyway.
